paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.

model_annotations.English: The vertical bar chart, titled "QAdapter," illustrates the number of FLOPs associated with different computational methods. The horizontal axis displays the categories, with labels rotated diagonally, ordered from left to right as Full FT, TAG, Adapter, MTL-FT, QAdapter, and Ours. The vertical axis, labeled "# FLOPs," utilizes a logarithmic scale with a visible range starting just below $10^{18}$ and extending up to $10^{20}$, featuring major tick labels at intervals of powers of ten ($10^{18}$, $10^{19}$, and $10^{20}$) along with corresponding light gray horizontal gridlines. The chart consists of six individual bars that follow a generally descending height trend from left to right, with a slight increase at the final category. The first five bars are colored orange, starting with the tallest bar for "Full FT" at an approximate value of $6 \times 10^{19}$. This is followed by "TAG" at roughly $2 \times 10^{19}$, "Adapter" at approximately $1.5 \times 10^{19}$, and "MTL-FT" at near $4 \times 10^{18}$. The shortest bar in the chart belongs to "QAdapter" at approximately $2 \times 10^{18}$. The final category, "Ours," is visually emphasized with a bolded axis text label and a distinct green bar, reaching an approximate value of $2.5 \times 10^{18}$.
model_annotations.German: The bar chart, titled "QAdapter," illustrates the computation cost associated with various fine-tuning methods. The horizontal axis contains the categorical methods, whose labels are rotated diagonally without an overarching axis title. The categories are positioned from left to right as "Full FT," "TAG," "Adapter," "MTL-FT," "QAdapter," and "Ours." The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "# FLOPs," and utilizes a logarithmic scale. The displayed value range spans from 10^18 to 10^20, with numeric tick labels and corresponding faint horizontal grid lines occurring at intervals of one power of 10. The chart features six individual vertical bars that generally follow a descending order in height from left to right, with the exception of the final category. The first five bars are colored solid orange. Among these, the "Full FT" bar is the tallest in the chart, reaching an approximate value of 6 x 10^19 FLOPs. The values then decrease for "TAG" (roughly 2 x 10^19 FLOPs), "Adapter" (slightly below TAG), and "MTL-FT" (approximately 4 x 10^18 FLOPs), leading to "QAdapter," which is the shortest bar overall with an approximate value of 2 x 10^18 FLOPs. The final bar, "Ours," has an approximate value of 2.2 x 10^18 FLOPs, making it slightly taller than "QAdapter." This final category is visually emphasized in two distinct ways: the bar is colored solid green to contrast with the orange bars, and its corresponding label on the horizontal axis is bolded.
